content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sodium canned bean soup is a ready‑to‑eat soup made from selected dry beans, vegetables, and spices. The canning process preserves flavor and nutrients while significantly lowering added salt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans are one of the oldest cultivated legumes, grown by humans for over 7,000 years.
Canning allows the product to be stored for 2‑3 years without quality loss.
Sodium reduction is achieved by using natural flavor enhancers and spices instead of salt.
Bean soup is considered a comfort food in many cultures, from the United States to Russia.
Legumes are rich in plant protein and fiber, making them an excellent choice for vegetarians.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Beans provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt is beneficial for individuals monitoring blood pressure.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals contribute to hemoglobin formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: B‑vitamins and antioxidants in beans help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Certain recipes may add sugar or sweeteners; diabetics should check the label.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: While most brands avoid artificial preservatives, some may use additives that cause sensitivity.

items.title: Proper heating
items.content: The soup should be heated to a rolling boil to eliminate any possible bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the soup in the microwave or on the stove for about 5‑7 minutes. It can be garnished with fresh herbs, served with crusty bread, or paired with boiled potatoes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 3‑4 days.
